what_happened: After landing changes to Athena's own code, the operator did not re-run setup, so the installed athena binary stayed on the old build while the checked-out source was newer. An audit (pg90) then ran on the old code and its result was void. Separately, the operator twice let the lease lapse, and that blocked pushes. The event is logged as an intervention with no job attached.
cause: Athena does not compare the build it is running with the source it runs against. Updating the installed binary after a self-landing depends on the operator remembering to re-run setup, and nothing flags a stale binary before an audit or job starts. The lease has the same weakness: it expires silently, and nothing warns or renews it before pushes are blocked. Both are protected only by the operator's memory.
prevention: Embed the source revision in the binary at build time. At the start of every job, audit and push, compare it with the checked-out source's revision. If the binary is older, refuse to start, or at least warn loudly and mark the result as not valid. Make a self-landing that changes Athena's code either rebuild and reinstall the binary automatically or print the exact setup command to run. Also check the lease's remaining time before long operations and warn, or renew it, when it is close to expiring.
proposed_request: Make Athena detect when its installed binary is older than the source it runs against, and warn about a lease that is about to lapse. Outcome: (1) the binary records the source revision it was built from. Every job, audit and push start compares that with the checked-out source. If they differ, Athena refuses to run, or marks the result void, and says which setup command to run. A test shows a stale binary is caught. (2) After a landing that changes Athena's own code, Athena either reinstalls the binary or prints the exact setup step. (3) Before a push or long operation, Athena checks how long the lease has left and warns when it is near expiry, with a test for that warning. Do not change unrelated behavior.
